profile_headline: Assistant Manager Finance at VKL Seasoning Pvt Ltd
post_content:
A highly polished stone and an ordinary sponge were hired by a firm; the
polished stone awed everyone, unlike the sponge. Both were good at their jobs,
no difference there. The polished stone would go about stamping all the work
it has done with its signature, and anyway because of its aura, its work was
more noticeable than the sponge on most occasions. The stone's self-worth
increased dramatically over time and had the propensity to leave the firm for
a place where it was paid equal to its value. It was not surprising that it
resigned soon after. Meanwhile, the ordinary sponge, being what it was,
absorbed all it could from its peers, got better by the day and started
hardening up like a stone. The firm could observe the progress and did all it
could to provide a conducive environment for the sponge to learn. Over time,
the sponge emerged as a polished stone, not unlike the one it had hired. Only,
having been transformed by the firm, the sponge-turned-stone had little
incentive to leave it. hashtag#learning hashtag#talentmanagement
hashtag#knowledgemanagement hashtag#officetruths Do comment on what you feel
about the above parable.

profile_headline: Associate Professor--Media Business+Mgmt;Marketing+Advertising; Film Finance+Marketing; Entrepreneurship;Media Economics
Product @ Internshala | Ex - Frontbench| Ed-Tech Enthusiast | Guest Writer at Leading Digital Platforms
post_content:
Lokesh Gupta always comes up with very interesting observations and this
should excite data science enthusiast. He says that Truecaller stores millions
of mobile users data. Every user can have multiple names from other user
contact's address. Like, my number can be as :- +91-xxxxxxxxx ----> Venkatesh
Frontbench +91-xxxxxxxxx ----> Venkatesh +91-xxxxxxxxx ----> Venkatesh Friend
+91-xxxxxxxxx ----> Venkatesh Beta So, how would one decide which name to show
from multiple names? Which name to trust and find meaning from it? I was
suddenly reminded of the two techniques I had studied in Natural Language
Processing a month ago - Stemming & Lemmatization. The goal of both of them is
to reduce infectional forms and sometimes derivationally related forms of a
word to a common base form. For instance:- am, are, is ---> be car, cars,
car's, cars' --> car Venkatesh, Venkatesh Friend, Venkatesh Frontbench,
Venkatesh Beta, Idiot Venkatesh --> Venkatesh You can know more about stemming
and lemmatization from here:- https://lnkd.in/fmQqjRk https://lnkd.in/fnNCgxh
